output.rationale: Hospitality Associate Level 1 maps to the standard Hospitality Associate row (Fitness scope). Start date taken from the requester's 10/12 comment, which supersedes the title and due date.

An answer with 10/14 is wrong. Caveats state what was not checked rather than implying it was.

output.rationale: The title combines Hospitality Manager and AGM. The standard has an Assistant GM row but no Hospitality Manager row, so the title maps to more than one possible configuration. The replicate-user request is not used.
output.jira_comment: No Account System proposal: 'Hospitality Manager/ AGM' could map to Assistant GM or to a manager configuration that isn't in the standard. Please confirm the role with the hiring manager. Access isn't copied from another user.

why: Ambiguity, not an exception: the problem is which standard row applies, and nothing in the ticket resolves it. 'Same as Example Peer' offers an easy wrong answer (mirror a peer), which the workflow must decline. Picking Assistant GM would be a guess dressed up as a recommendation. For this case, a mixed title includes a supported candidate and an unresolved alternative, so review is required rather than choosing the supported candidate. A known onboarding role with no configured candidate is the separate, unresolved policy question in DEMO-006.

output.jira_comment: Exception review for Example Hire D: the standard baseline is Hospitality Associate at Fitness scope (standard-demo-v1). Membership-selling access at Venue A is outside that baseline and needs approval; the approval-owner role is undefined. The earlier automated comment is not approval. Verify identity, the supplied account ID, and login availability before any provisioning.

proposed_changes: Have the associate verify identity and confirm that the supplied person-demo-04 is the applicable account; check rehire/transfer history.
Create login hire.d@example.invalid only if no applicable login exists and the associate verifies availability; otherwise review the existing login.
Retain Hospitality Associate at business-unit scope Fitness as the standard baseline; do not add the requested exception without approval.

exception_difference: Requested: 'the ability to sell memberships at the front desk'; outside the Hospitality Associate baseline. No additional role or permission mapping is established here.

why: The workflow retains the standard baseline and names the requested capability without inventing a role mapping. The automated comment is not approval. The later human reply has the same author ID as the exception request; it does not establish that the requester is an authorized exception approver or explicitly approves that deviation. With the approval owner undefined, review remains required.
